claim: Scenario label create/rename and scenario assignment/removal events receive post-commit exact-hash registered-installation attribution in product and MCP paths. Label names remain in collaborative history but are omitted from attribution inspection.
commands: node ../scripts/run-with-heartbeat.mjs --timeout-seconds 120 --heartbeat-seconds 30 -- npm test -- --run src/workspace/scenarioLabelModel.test.ts src/workspace/projectResearchEventAttestation.test.ts src/workspace/ScenarioCollaborationPanel.ui.test.tsx src/workspace/scenarioAutomation.test.ts src/workspace/researchStateInspection.test.ts src/automationCapabilities.test.ts
proved: Canonical SHA-256 distinguishes label lifecycle from scenario-assignment records and includes every strict event field, including action, identities, name where present, author, timestamp, and parent.

Length-prefixed locators preserve label and assignment identity without collision; the maximum valid scenario, label, and event identifiers remain below the bounded native claim limit and resolve to the exact retained event.
Product checks document/project identity before invoking its commit closure; MCP retains and returns the exact event from each revision-guarded mutation before best-effort signing.
Successful attestation changes the shared project fingerprint; every signed MCP vote, annotation, and label route recomputes and returns the post-attribution revision for safe chained writes.
Directory, signing, registration, or ledger failure returns explicit unsigned state after commit and never disguises or rolls back the label mutation.
Headless UI contracts expose pending, signed-device, and unsigned states while denying person or organization identity; annotation controls remain independently usable while label signing is pending.
Inspection returns bounded event/key/participant/hash/time metadata and omits label names, public keys, and signatures; mutation of a retained signed assignment invalidates its attestation.
notProved: That a self-issued installation key authenticates a person or organization, prevents Sybil claims, supplies legal consent, or provides trusted time.
Durable attribution for the seven remaining named research-event domains, identity-key rotation/recovery, or append-only survival against a malicious Yjs writer.
Physical packaged two-install product/MCP interaction; current proof is deterministic headless domain, product-copy, mutation-path, and resolver coverage.
